Subject: Prompt output retention & SLA exceptions for Slate Health

Hi Evan / Priya —

Great to meet you both on the product discovery call today. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups so we have alignment before looping legal/procurement: 

- Recap: Slate Health will evaluate Redwood for embedding and chat features in the patient triage flow. Primary concerns today were: PII appearing in prompt inputs, retention of generated outputs, and audit/logging available for compliance reviews.

- What we agreed on the call: Redwood can run in a configuration where raw prompt text is not persisted to disk in production (ephemeral capture). Prompt derivatives (model outputs + minimal metadata) can be retained for a configurable TTL and exported for audits.

As next steps, can you confirm the following so we can prepare a narrow MPA redline and an ops runbook?
1) Required retention window for prompt outputs (days): production vs sandbox.
2) Whether hashed-only storage of any identifiers (e.g., MRN, email) would be acceptable for logs/audit extracts.
3) Any mandatory region/legal requirements (we noted US only today).

I attached: a lightweight dataflow diagram (redwood-dataflow-v1.png) and a draft MPA redline we often start from (draft-MPA-redline-v1.pdf). I’ll loop Rishi on the technical workso he can confirm the exact logging/TTL options and which fields we can sink to your SIEM.

Thanks — looking forward to the confirmation.

Best,

Laura —

Thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick answers while we confirm with security/legal:

- Retention: target is 30 days for production prompt outputs; sandbox can be 7 days. We may need a path to request shorter windows for specific datasets.
- Hashed-only identifiers: yes, hashed identifiers are preferable for audit exports. We would like to avoid storing raw MRNs/emails in any persistent store.
- Region: US (no EU data).

Two asks from our side: 1) can Redwood provide a sample audit extract (anonymized) demonstrating the fields included; 2) we will need a clear SLA exception for token-level logging for 3rd-party debugging purposes — who at Redwood signs that?

Appreciate Rishi joining on the technical details.

—Evan

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Prompt output retention & SLA exceptions for Slate Health

Hi Evan / Priya —

Thanks for the quick answers. Technical clarification and what we can commit to in the MPA redline: 

- Retention configuration: Redwood supports per-route TTL for prompt derivatives. We can set production flows to 30 days (default auto-delete job) and sandbox to 7 days. TTLs are configurable in the workspace and can be overridden only by an explicit signed exception.

- Ephemeral/persistence options: raw prompt text can be configured as ephemeral-only (kept in-memory and not written to persistent KV). The runtime uses KV-cache for tokens during generation; by default that cache is in-memory and not persisted to disk. For customers requiring zero-persist, we have a "no-persist" mode that disables write-through logging of prompt bodies.

- Audit extracts: we can produce an anonymized CSV with the following columns: request_id, route, timestamp (UTC), redacted_user_id (SHA-256), model_variant, output_snippet (first 200 chars), error_flag. I attached a sample retention-matrix.csv showing fields and default TTLs.

- SLA exceptions & sign-off: for token-level logging (for onboarding debugging), our Security/Legal team signs a scoped SLA exception limited in time and purpose. Ben (cc'ed) is our Sales Ops contact to coordinate the procurement/legal paperwork; he can route to Security.

- Evidence: SOC2 attestation (SOC2-Attestation-2026.pdf) is attached for your compliance team.

If 30 days + hashed identifiers works for you, Laura and I will prepare a narrow MPA redline and a one-page ops runbook describing the retention job, export process, and who to contact for emergency debug access.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Attachments: retention-matrix.csv (csv, 12 KB); SOC2-Attestation-2026.pdf (pdf, 1.1 MB)

Laura / Rishi —

Confirming on behalf of Slate Health: 30 days retention for production prompt outputs, 7 days for sandbox. Hashed-only identifiers acceptable for audit exports (SHA-256 ok). Region: US-only.

Next steps from our side: legal will review the draft MPA redline — please send the narrow redline (we prefer PDF + DocuSign link). Also need the anonymized sample audit extract for Security to review (the CSV Rishi referenced is perfect).

We will expect an SLA exception template for token-level logging limited to a 14-day window for debugging that requires Security approval. Please include Ben in procurement/ops coordination.

Thanks — Priya
